nahhas-irab:1-1.t: «تَبارَكَ»: the experts in the language have spoken about its meaning. Al-Farrāʾ said: in Arabic it and تقدّس ("He is hallowed") are one and the same, and both express majesty. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: it is the form tafāʿala from al-baraka ("blessing"). He said: the meaning of al-baraka is abundance of everything good. It has been said: تبارك means "He is exalted" (تعالى); and it has been said: the meaning is "His giving is exalted", i.e. it has increased and become abundant; and it has been said: the meaning is "His favours have endured and remained firm". This last is the most fitting of them in the language, the derivation being from برك الشيء ("the thing stayed firm"), and from it برك الجمل ("the camel knelt down [and stayed]"). As for the first view, it is muddled, because التقديس comes only from purity, and this has nothing to do with that. «الَّذِي نَزَّلَ الْفُرْقانَ» is in the position of the nominative (marfūʿ) by its verb. «الفرقان» is the Qur'an, because it distinguishes (farraqa) between truth and falsehood, and between the believer and the unbeliever. «عَلى عَبْدِهِ»: so that [the pronoun in «ليكون»] refers to him; it may also refer to «الفرقان». One says أنذر ("he warned") when he caused fear, and «نذير» is for intensiveness.

nahhas-irab:2-2.t:
«الَّذِي لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ» is in the position of the nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of, or a badal (substitute) for, the «الذي» before it.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «فَقَدْ جاؤُ ظُلْماً», i.e. "with wrongdoing" (بظلم). Someone else said: [it means] "they have brought wrongdoing and falsehood".

nahhas-irab:5-5.t: «وَقالُوا أَساطِيرُ الْأَوَّلِينَ»: on the basis of an implied mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "and they said: what you have brought is the tales of the ancients". Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: its singular is أسطورة, like أحدوثة and أحاديث. Someone else said: «أساطير» is the plural of أسطار, like أقوال and أقاويل. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah have mercy on him, that the one who said this was al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, and likewise everything in the Qur'an in which the tales (al-asāṭīr) are mentioned. Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq said: he used to harm the Prophet ﷺ. «اكْتَتَبَها فَهِيَ تُمْلى عَلَيْهِ»: according to the dialect of those who say أملى; those who say أملّ say تملّ عليه. «بُكْرَةً وَأَصِيلًا».

nahhas-irab:7-7.t: «وَقالُوا مالِ هذَا الرَّسُولِ»: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «ما» is separate. The meaning is: what is the matter with this messenger in his walking and his eating? «لَوْلا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ», i.e. "why not" (هلّا). «فَيَكُونَ مَعَهُ نَذِيراً» is the answer to the question.

nahhas-irab:8-8.t: «أَوْ يُلْقى» is in the position of the nominative, and the meaning is: "or why is a treasure not cast down to him", or "why does he not have" «تَكُونُ لَهُ جَنَّةٌ يَأْكُلُ مِنْها»: this is the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim. The Kufans read «نَأْكُلَ مِنْها» with nūn. Both readings are good and convey two meanings, though the reading with yāʾ is clearer, because the Prophet ﷺ alone has been mentioned before, so that the pronoun referring back to him is clearer.

nahhas-irab:9-9.t: «انْظُرْ كَيْفَ ضَرَبُوا لَكَ الْأَمْثالَ», i.e. they struck these comparisons for you so as to arrive at calling you a liar, «فَضَلُّوا» from the path of truth and from attaining what they wanted, «فَلا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ سَبِيلًا», i.e. [a way] to making good what they said about you.

nahhas-irab:10-10.t: «تَبارَكَ الَّذِي إِنْ شاءَ جَعَلَ لَكَ خَيْراً مِنْ ذلِكَ»: a condition and its requital. It is not assimilated [i.e. the lām of «جعل» into the lām of «لك»] because the two words are separate, though assimilation is permissible because two identical letters meet. «وَيَجْعَلْ لَكَ قُصُوراً» is in the position of the jussive (majzūm), conjoined to the position of «جعل»; it may also be in the position of the nominative, conjoined to the first two, and then assimilated. Al-Farrāʾ permitted the accusative on the basis of al-ṣarf ("diversion"). The people of Syria read — and it is also related from ʿĀṣim — «وَيَجْعَلْ لَكَ قُصُوراً» with the nominative, i.e. "and He will make for you palaces in the Hereafter".

nahhas-irab:13-13.t: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «ثُبُوراً» is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "we have perished a perishing" (ثبرنا ثبورا). Someone else said: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "they called on destruction", just as one says يا عجباه ("O wonder!"), i.e. "this is your time, so be present", and this is more eloquent than تعجّبت ("I was amazed").

nahhas-irab:14-14.t: I.e. your affliction is greater than that you should call on destruction just once; rather they will call on it many times. «الثبور» is not put in the plural because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-irab:15-15.t:
Just as Sībawayh relates from the Arabs: الشّقاء أحبّ إليك أم السعادة؟ ("Is misery dearer to you, or happiness?"), when it is known that happiness is dearer to him. It has been said: this is for drawing attention; and it has been said: the meaning is "is that good?" without the sense of «من» [i.e. not as a comparative], just as one says عنده خير ("he has good"). This is a good view, as [the poet] said: [al-wāfir] 309-
فشرّكما لخيركما الفداء
(So the worse of you two is a ransom for the better of you two.)
There is a third view on the verse, namely that the Kufans permit العسل أحلى من الخل ("honey is sweeter than vinegar"). This view is rejected, because the meaning of "so-and-so is better than so-and-so" is that he has more good than him, and there is no sweetness in vinegar. Nor may you say "the Christian is better than the Jew", because there is no good in either of them so that one of them should exceed the other in good; rather one says "the Jew is worse than the Christian". This is how the speech of the Arabs goes.

nahhas-irab:18-18.t: Al-Ḥasan and Abū Jaʿfar read «أن نتّخذ» with ḍamma on the nūn [i.e. أن نُتَّخَذ, "that we be taken"]. The grammarians have discussed this reading and agreed that the fatḥa on the nūn is preferable. Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar said: (نُتّخذ) is not permissible. Abū ʿAmr said: had it been «نُتّخذ», the second (من) would have been dropped, and you would say: أن نُتّخذ من دونك أولياء. That one such as Abū ʿAmr, with his eminence and standing, should say this is to be appreciated, because he has brought a clear reason. The explanation of what he said is that one says ما اتّخذت رجلا وليّا ("I did not take a man as a protector"), and this may apply to one particular individual; then one says ما اتخذت من رجل وليّا ("I did not take any man as a protector"), and it is a general negation. Your word «وليّا» follows what precedes it, so «من» may not enter it, because there is no point in that. Al-Farrāʾ related from the Arabs that they do not say ما رأيت عبد الله من رجل, but he then invalidated this, abandoned what he had related from the Arabs, and permitted it on his own account, saying: if they meant ما رأيت من رجل عبد الله, it would be permissible to insert «من», interpreting it as an inversion (al-qalb). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: this is a mistake and is not permissible at all — and it is as he said. Then al-Farrāʾ went back and said: the Arabs insert «من» only before nouns — and this is a clear contradiction. Al-Kisāʾī also permitted it, then said: it is ugly. «وَلكِنْ مَتَّعْتَهُمْ وَآباءَهُمْ», i.e. their lives grew long after the death of the messengers, Allah's blessings be upon them, so they forgot and perished.

nahhas-irab:19-19.t: «فَقَدْ كَذَّبُوكُمْ بِما تَقُولُونَ»: Abū ʿUbayd interpreted it in the sense of "in what they say". Someone else said: this is an address to the prophets, Allah bless them and grant them peace. «فما تستطيعون صرفا ولا نصرا»: it has been said: they are not able to turn the punishment away from themselves, nor to help one another.

nahhas-irab:20-20.t:
When the lām enters, «إنّ» can only have kasra; and even if there were no lām, only kasra would be permissible, because it begins a new clause. This is the view of all the grammarians, except that ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān related to us from Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] that he said: fatḥa is permissible in this «إنّ» even though the lām comes after it — and I think that was an error on his part. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is "We did not send before you messengers except that they ate food"; then «من» was omitted, because «من» indicates what is omitted. Al-Farrāʾ said: «من» is omitted, i.e. "except that among them there were those who ate food", and he compared it to His saying «وَما مِنَّا إِلَّا لَهُ مَقامٌ مَعْلُومٌ» [al-Ṣāffāt: 164].
Abū Isḥāq said: this is a mistake, because «من» is a relative (mawṣūla), so it may not be omitted. «وَجَعَلْنا بَعْضَكُمْ لِبَعْضٍ فِتْنَةً»: al-fitna in the language is testing, and in the hadith: "The rich man is a trial for the poor and the poor a trial for the rich; the strong is a trial for the weak and the weak a trial for the strong." The meaning of this is that each of the two is tested by his companion: the rich man is tested by the poor — he must console him and not mock him — and the poor man is tried by the rich — he must not envy him and must take from him only what he gives him — and each of them must be patient upon the truth, as al-Ḍaḥḥāk said on the meaning of «أَتَصْبِرُونَ»: i.e. upon the truth. «وَكانَ رَبُّكَ بَصِيراً», i.e. of what you do, i.e. in that with which He tried you.

nahhas-irab:22-22.t:
«يوم يرون» may not be accusative by «بشرى», because what is in the predicate of wonder or in the predicate of negation does not govern what precedes it. But there are two possible constructions here: the meaning may be "they are denied the good tidings on the day they see the angels", what follows indicating this omission; or the construction may be "there will be no good tidings «يوم يرون الملائكة»", with «يومئذ» as tawkīd (emphasis). It may also be that the meaning is "remember the day they see the angels".
«وَيَقُولُونَ حِجْراً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a prohibition"; from it comes حجرت على فلان ("I placed so-and-so under restriction"), and from it حجرة ("room") was said.

nahhas-irab:23-23.t: I.e. it is of no benefit, i.e. We have made it void. «هباء» is not one of the words with hamza [as a root letter]; it was given a hamza only because of the meeting of two quiescent letters. The diminutive is هبيّ in the position of the nominative, and among the grammarians there are some who say هبيّ in the position of the nominative. [Translator's note: translated as printed; the two forms are identical in the text as transmitted, so the difference between the two views appears to have been lost in the source.]

nahhas-irab:24-24.t:
«أَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَئِذٍ خَيْرٌ مُسْتَقَرًّا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and a khabar (predicate). We have mentioned something like it before this, in «أَذلِكَ خَيْرٌ أَمْ جَنَّةُ الْخُلْدِ» [al-Furqān: 15], and we related the view of the Kufans that they permit العسل أحلى من الخلّ ("honey is sweeter than vinegar"). Al-Farrāʾ mentioned on this verse more than this: he claimed that the meaning is:
"The companions of the Garden on that day are better in abode than the people of the Fire", while there is no good in the abode of the people of the Fire — so it is as if he refuted himself. I heard ʿAlī ibn Sulaymān say on this, relating it, that the meaning is: since you used to do the deeds of the people of the Fire, you became as though you were saying that there is good in that. It has been said: better in abode than what you are in; and it has been said: «خير» not in the sense of afʿal [the comparative], with «مستقرّ» then being an adverb (ẓarf); on what preceded, it is accusative as an explanation (bayān, i.e. tamyīz).

nahhas-irab:25-25.t: «وَيَوْمَ تَشَقَّقُ السَّماءُ بِالْغَمامِ»: the original form is تتشقّق; the tāʾ was assimilated into the shīn. The Kufans read «تَشَقَّقُ» [with a single shīn]: they omitted the tāʾ because the remaining tāʾ indicates it.

nahhas-irab:26-26.t: «الْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ الْحَقُّ لِلرَّحْمنِ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and a khabar (predicate). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] permitted the accusative of «الحقّ» in the sense of "I affirm the truth" or "I mean the truth". «وَكانَ يَوْماً عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ عَسِيراً»: its verb is عسر يعسر and عسر يعسر.

nahhas-irab:27-27.t: «وَيَوْمَ يَعَضُّ الظَّالِمُ عَلى يَدَيْهِ»: the past tense is عضضت, and al-Kisāʾī related عضَضت with fatḥa on the first ḍād. Authoritative report has come from the people of exegesis, among them Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, that the wrongdoer here is ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ and that his close friend is Umayya ibn Khalaf. ʿUqba was killed by ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, and Umayya was killed by the Prophet ﷺ. This was one of the proofs of the Prophet ﷺ, because he gave news of the two of them with this, and they were killed in unbelief. They are not named in the verse because that is more effective in conveying the lesson, so that it be known that this is the way of every wrongdoer who accepts from another [a call] to disobey Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

nahhas-irab:28-28.t:
«يا وَيْلَتى»: al-Ḥasan read «يا ويلتي» with yāʾ. The first reading is more common in the speech of the Arabs, because they omit when they say يا غلام أقبل ("O boy, come forward"), since the vocative is a place of omission. Al-Aṣmaʿī used to recite Zuhayr's verse: [al-ṭawīl] 310-
تبصّر خليل هل ترى من ظعائن ... تحمّلن بالعلياء من فوق جرثم
(Look, O friend: do you see any women in litters who have loaded up on the heights above Jurthum?)
and he rejected the version of those who relate «تبصّر خليلي», because he aimed at the sound, eloquent versions and did not turn aside to the irregular. Likewise the experts of the language relate: [al-basīṭ] 311-
قالت هريرة لمّا جئت زائرها ... ويلا عليك وويلا منك يا رجل
(Hurayra said, when I came to visit her: "Woe upon you, and woe from you, O man!")

nahhas-irab:30-30.t: «الْقُرْآنَ» is a naʿt (adjective) of «هذا», because «هذا» is qualified by what has the alif and lām, even if it is not formed from a verb. «مَهْجُوراً» is a second object.

nahhas-irab:31-32.t: «وَكَذلِكَ جَعَلْنا لِكُلِّ نَبِيٍّ عَدُوًّا»: the kāf is in the position of the accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun); likewise the kāf in «كَذلِكَ لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِ فُؤادَكَ», the meaning being "a strengthening like that strengthening". This is on the basis that the complete stop is at His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «جُمْلَةً واحِدَةً»; if the complete stop is at «كذلك», the construction is "a measured recitation like that". This is because, when the idolaters found no way to call the Prophet ﷺ a liar by any proof or argument, they said «لَوْلا نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ الْقُرْآنُ جُمْلَةً واحِدَةً», so they asked for something in which the right course lay elsewhere, because the Qur'an used to be sent down piecemeal in answer to what they asked about, and that was one of the signs of prophethood, because they would not ask about anything without being answered about it. This can come only from a prophet, so it was a strengthening of his heart and of their hearts, and the answer points to this.

nahhas-irab:33-33.t:
Had it been sent down all at once, it would have preceded the events concerning which the Qur'an used to be sent down; and had it been sent down all at once with the obligations it contains, that would have weighed heavily on them. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew that the right course lay in sending it down in parts, because they are alerted by it time after time, whereas had it been sent down all at once, the sense of alerting would have disappeared. It also contains abrogating and abrogated [passages]: they would be bound to worship by a thing up to a particular time in which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knew the right course lay, and then the abrogation would be sent down after that; so it is impossible that "do such-and-such" and "do not do it" should be sent down all at once. It is preferable that the complete stop be at «جملة واحدة», because if one stops at «كذلك», the meaning becomes "like the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms", and these have not been mentioned before. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «وَرَتَّلْناهُ تَرْتِيلًا», i.e. "We sent it down". It has been said:
al-tartīl is unhurriedness, and it is the opposite of haste.

nahhas-irab:34-34.t:
«الَّذِينَ يُحْشَرُونَ عَلى وُجُوهِهِمْ إِلى جَهَنَّمَ» is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is in the clause.
We have mentioned its meaning as related in a report traced back to the Prophet. It has also been said: it is a figure of speech, as you say "he came to me on his face", i.e. unwillingly.

nahhas-irab:35-35.t: «وَجَعَلْنا مَعَهُ أَخاهُ هارُونَ»: as a badal (substitute). «وَزِيراً» is a second object. «الوزير» in the language is the helper to whom his master resorts, derived from al-wazar, which is a place of refuge. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: «كَلَّا لا وَزَرَ» [al-Qiyāma: 11].

nahhas-irab:36-36.t:
Al-Farrāʾ said: in meaning, Moses ﷺ alone was ordered to go, and this is like His saying
«نَسِيا حُوتَهُما» [al-Kahf: 61], and like His saying «يَخْرُجُ مِنْهُمَا اللُّؤْلُؤُ وَالْمَرْجانُ» [al-Raḥmān: 22], when they come out of only one of the two. Abū Jaʿfar said: this is the kind of thing with which one ought not to be bold against the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and He, exalted be His praise, has said: «فَقُولا لَهُ قَوْلًا لَيِّناً لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ أَوْ يَخْشى قالا رَبَّنا إِنَّنا نَخافُ أَنْ يَفْرُطَ عَلَيْنا أَوْ أَنْ يَطْغى» [Ṭā Hā: 44, 45]. The parallel of this is in His saying
«وَمِنْ دُونِهِما جَنَّتانِ» [al-Raḥmān: 62], and He, exalted be His praise, has said: «ثُمَّ أَرْسَلْنا مُوسى وَأَخاهُ هارُونَ بِآياتِنا» [al-Muʾminūn: 45].

nahhas-irab:37-37.t:
«وَقَوْمَ نُوحٍ»: there are several views on its accusative: it may be conjoined to the pronoun in «فَدَمَّرْناهُمْ»; or it may be in the sense of "and remember"; or it may be by an implied verb explained by what follows, the construction being "and We drowned the people of Noah".
These are three views. Al-Farrāʾ claimed that it is accusative by «أغرقناهم», but this does not hold, because أغرقنا is not one of the verbs that take two objects so that it could govern both the pronoun and «قوم نوح».

nahhas-irab:38-38.t: All of this may be conjoined to «قوم نوح» if «قوم نوح» is accusative by conjunction or in the sense of "and remember". All of this may also be accusative as conjoined to the pronoun in «وَجَعَلْناهُمْ», and that is preferable because it is nearer to it.

nahhas-irab:39-39.t: «وَكُلًّا ضَرَبْنا لَهُ الْأَمْثالَ»: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: "and He warned each". He said: al-tatbīr is destruction, and from it broken glass is called tibr, and likewise tibr of gold.

nahhas-irab:40-40.t:
It has been said: this is about the unbelievers who disbelieved in the Prophet ﷺ, because they had come upon the cities of the people of Lot, peace be upon him, and knew that they were destroyed for their unbelief. «أَفَلَمْ يَكُونُوا يَرَوْنَها بَلْ كانُوا لا يَرْجُونَ نُشُوراً»: whoever denies [the existence of] words with opposite meanings (al-aḍdād) says that «يرجون» has its usual sense [of hoping], because they disbelieved in the Hereafter only out of rejection of the truth, not out of certainty, so they do not hope for it. Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] was one of those who denied al-aḍdād, and he said:
the meaning is: rather they did not hope for the reward of the resurrection, so they were bold in committing sins.

nahhas-irab:41-41.t: «وَإِذا رَأَوْكَ إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ»: the answer to «إِذا» is «إِنْ يَتَّخِذُونَكَ إِلَّا هُزُواً», because its meaning is "they take you". It has been said: the answer is omitted, because the meaning is: they said, "Is this the one whom He sent?" «الَّذِي بَعَثَ اللَّهُ رَسُولًا»: «رسول» is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); it may also be a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of بعث is أرسل ("sent"), and «رسول» on this view means "a message".

nahhas-irab:43-43.t: «أَفَأَنْتَ تَكُونُ عَلَيْهِ وَكِيلًا»: it has been said that its meaning is: would you then compel him to that?

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: «أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ أَوْ يَعْقِلُونَ»: He did not say "that they", because among them there were some of whom He knew that they would believe. He, Mighty and Majestic, censured them with this: «أَمْ تَحْسَبُ أَنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ يَسْمَعُونَ» with a hearing of acceptance, or reflect on what you say and so understand it, i.e. they are in the position of one who neither understands nor hears. It has been said: the meaning is that since they did not benefit from what they heard, it is as if they did not hear. «إِنْ هُمْ إِلَّا كَالْأَنْعامِ», i.e. they do not comprehend. «بَلْ هُمْ أَضَلُّ سَبِيلًا», because they deny the truth they hear, and cattle are not like that.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: «أَلَمْ تَرَ إِلى رَبِّكَ»: the alif was omitted because of the jussive. The origin has hamza, and the lightening [of the hamza] is obligatory in the imperfect of this [verb] because of its frequent use. We have already mentioned the meaning of the verse.

nahhas-irab:47-49.t: «وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ اللَّيْلَ لِباساً»: two objects. «وَالنَّوْمَ سُباتاً» is conjoined, and «سبات» means rest. «جعل» was repeated for tawkīd (emphasis); had it been «والنهار نشورا» [without repeating the verb], it would be permissible outside the Qur'an. Al-Akhfash Saʿīd said: the singular of «الأناسيّ» is إنسيّ, and Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said the same; it is one of al-Farrāʾ's two views. He has another view, namely that the singular of «الأناسيّ» is إنسان, with the nūn changed into yāʾ, so that one says أناسيّ; on his view he is obliged to say, in the plural of سرحان, سراحيّ — there is no difference between them. He also related «وَأَناسِيَ كَثِيراً» with the lightened [yāʾ].

nahhas-irab:50-50.t: «وَلَقَدْ صَرَّفْناهُ بَيْنَهُمْ»: it is the rain, as ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd and ʿAbdallāh ibn ʿAbbās said: no year has more rain than another year, but Allah directs it wherever He wills. «فَأَبى أَكْثَرُ النَّاسِ إِلَّا كُفُوراً»: no disagreement is known among the people of exegesis that the unbelief here is their saying "We were given rain by such-and-such a star", and that its parallel is the astrologer's saying "the star did such-and-such", and that everyone who attributes an action to them is an unbeliever.

nahhas-irab:54-54.t: «وَهُوَ الَّذِي خَلَقَ مِنَ الْماءِ بَشَراً فَجَعَلَهُ نَسَباً وَصِهْراً»: the scholars have three views on this. The most eminent of them is what is related from Ibn ʿAbbās; he said: the kinship by lineage (al-nasab) is seven: «حُرِّمَتْ عَلَيْكُمْ أُمَّهاتُكُمْ وَبَناتُكُمْ وَأَخَواتُكُمْ وَعَمَّاتُكُمْ وَخالاتُكُمْ وَبَناتُ الْأَخِ وَبَناتُ الْأُخْتِ» [al-Nisāʾ: 23], and the kinship by marriage (al-ṣihr) is the seven: «وَأُمَّهاتُكُمُ اللَّاتِي أَرْضَعْنَكُمْ» [al-Nisāʾ: 23] to the end of the verse. The explanation of this is that the first seven are from lineage, so its construction in Arabic is "He made him possessed of lineage and possessed of marriage-kinship"; and the seven of marriage-kinship are those among whom marriage-kinship would occur were it not for what has arisen. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: al-nasab is the relatives, and al-ṣihr is those [women] related by suckling. The third view is that al-nasab is the male offspring and al-ṣihr the female offspring, because marriage-kinship comes about from two sides.

nahhas-irab:55-55.t: «وَكانَ الْكافِرُ عَلى رَبِّهِ ظَهِيراً»: it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that the unbeliever here is Abū Jahl and his partisans, because he sought the backing of the idol-worshippers against the friends of his Lord. ʿIkrima said: the unbeliever is Iblīs, a backer in enmity to his Lord. Maṭar said: the unbeliever here is Satan.

nahhas-irab:57-57.t: «مَنْ» is in the position of [and] the accusative as an exception not of the same kind as the first [i.e. a disjoined exception]. [Translator's note: the wording «في موضع ونصب» is translated as printed; «في موضع نصب» is evidently meant.] The construction is: "but whoever wishes to spend seeking the pleasure of Allah so as to take a way to the reward of his Lord, let him do so."

nahhas-irab:59-59.t: «ثُمَّ اسْتَوى عَلَى الْعَرْشِ الرَّحْمنُ»: there are three ways of explaining its nominative: it may be a badal (substitute) for the latent pronoun in «استوى»; it may be nominative in the sense of "He is the All-Merciful"; and it may be nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being «فَسْئَلْ بِهِ خَبِيراً». The genitive is also permissible, in the sense of "and rely on the Living One who does not die, the All-Merciful", being a naʿt (adjective); and the accusative is permissible as praise.

nahhas-irab:60-60.t: This is the reading of the Medinans and the Basrans; al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read «لما يأمرنا» with yāʾ. The first reading is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd, and he interpreted the second, as we see it, as "Shall we prostrate to what the All-Merciful commands us?" He said: had they acknowledged that the All-Merciful commanded them, they would not have been unbelievers. But this far-fetched interpretation ought not to be given on behalf of the Kufans in their reading; rather the better interpretation on their behalf is "Shall we prostrate to what the Prophet ﷺ commands us?", and the reading is sound on this basis, though the first is clearer and more readily understood.

nahhas-irab:61-61.t:
This is the reading of the Medinans, the Basrans and ʿĀṣim; the rest of the Kufans read «سرجا» ("lamps"). The first reading is preferable according to Abū ʿUbayd, because he interpreted that al-suruj are the stars and that al-burūj are the stars; but this ought not to be the interpretation given on their behalf, so that the meaning would come out as "stars and stars". Rather, the interpretation on their behalf is that Abān ibn Taghlib said: al-suruj are the brilliant stars. On this basis the reading is sound, and it is like His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «مَنْ كانَ عَدُوًّا لِلَّهِ وَمَلائِكَتِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَجِبْرِيلَ وَمِيكالَ» [al-Baqara: 98]: the shining stars are mentioned again, though the first reading is clearer and plainer in interpretation. Ibn ʿAbbās said: the lamp (al-sirāj) is the sun. ʿIṣma related from al-Aʿmash «وَقَمَراً» with ḍamma on the qāf and sukūn on the mīm [i.e. قُمْرا]. This is an irregular reading.
Even if there were nothing [against] it but that Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal — and he was the imam of the Muslims in his time — said: "Do not write down what this ʿIṣma who relates the readings narrates." Abū Ḥātim al-Sijistānī was fond of mentioning what this ʿIṣma relates. [Translator's note: the conditional sentence «ولو لم يكن فيها إلا أن…» is left without a main clause in the source; it is translated as it stands.]

nahhas-irab:62-62.t: «وَهُوَ الَّذِي جَعَلَ اللَّيْلَ وَالنَّهارَ خِلْفَةً لِمَنْ أَرادَ أَنْ يَذَّكَّرَ»: this is the reading of the Medinans, Abū ʿAmr, ʿĀṣim — with disagreement from him — and al-Kisāʾī. Al-Aʿmash and Ḥamza read «لِمَنْ أَرادَ أَنْ يَذَّكَّرَ» [i.e. أن يَذْكُرَ]. [Translator's note: both readings are printed identically in the source; the second is the lightened form يَذْكُرَ.] The original form of «يذّكّر» is يتذكّر; then the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl, i.e. he reflects and thinks on the creation of Allah, for the indication in it is clear — so this reading is clear. And «يذكر» may mean that these things become clear to him by his remembering [them].

nahhas-irab:63-63.t: «وَعِبادُ الرَّحْمنِ» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). This has been difficult for a group of grammarians, so much so that al-Akhfash said: it is a mubtadaʾ without a khabar (predicate), meaning that it is omitted. I have seen Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] bring on this something better than this view of al-Akhfash. He said: «عباد» is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, «الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ هَوْناً» is part of their description, «والذين» which comes after it is conjoined to it, and the khabar is «أُوْلئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ الْغُرْفَةَ» [al-Furqān: 75]. He said: the khabar may also be «الَّذِينَ يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ». «قالُوا سَلاماً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun). We have already mentioned its meaning.

nahhas-irab:66-66.t: «إِنَّها ساءَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا»: Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: «مستقرا» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), i.e. "in abode". The way of the tamyīz is that it contains the sense of «من», so the meaning is: "it is evil among abodes".

nahhas-irab:67-67.t:
«وَالَّذِينَ إِذا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا»: this is the reading of al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, ʿĀṣim and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb — with disagreement from the two of them — and it is a good reading, from قتر يقتُر, which is the regular pattern for the intransitive, like قعد يقعد. Abū ʿAmr read «لَمْ يَقْتُرُوا» [i.e. يَقْتِروا], and it is a well-known, good dialect form. The people of Medina read «وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا» [i.e. يُقْتِروا]. [Translator's note: the three readings are printed identically in the source; the bracketed vowelling follows the description in the text.] Abū Ḥātim was surprised at this reading of the people of Medina, because in his view the irregular does not occur in their reading, since one says أقتر يُقتر only when [someone] becomes poor, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: «وَعَلَى الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ» [al-Baqara: 236]. Abū Ḥātim interpreted it on their behalf as meaning that the spendthrift soon becomes poor; this is a far-fetched interpretation. Rather, the interpretation on their behalf is that Abū ʿUmar al-Jarmī related from al-Aṣmaʿī that one says of a person when he is stingy: قتر يقتُر and يقتِر, قتّر يقتّر, and أقتر يُقتر. On this basis the reading is sound, though the fatḥa on the yāʾ is sounder, more readily understood, better known and more familiar. Among the best things said about its meaning is what al-Ḥasan ibn Ghulayb related to us; he said: ʿImrān ibn Abī ʿImrān related to me; he said: Khallād ibn Sulaymān al-Ḥaḍramī related to us; he said: ʿAmr ibn Abī Labīd related to me from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥubulī, concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «وَالَّذِينَ إِذا أَنْفَقُوا لَمْ يُسْرِفُوا وَلَمْ يَقْتُرُوا وَكانَ بَيْنَ ذلِكَ قَواماً»: he said: whoever spends in other than obedience to Allah, that is extravagance; whoever withholds from obedience to Allah, that is stinginess; and whoever spends in obedience to Allah, that is the right measure (al-qawām). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: what truly explains this verse is the manners Allah, Mighty and Majestic, taught His Prophet ﷺ, saying: «وَلا تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إِلى عُنُقِكَ وَلا تَبْسُطْها كُلَّ الْبَسْطِ» [al-Isrāʾ: 29]. «وَكانَ بَيْنَ ذلِكَ قَواماً»: [«قواما»] is the khabar of kāna, and the noun of kāna is implied in it, indicated by «أنفقوا»; the construction is:
"the spending was, between extravagance and stinginess, a just mean". Al-Farrāʾ has another view, making «بين» the noun of kāna while leaving it in the accusative. Abū Jaʿfar said: I do not know what the justification of this is, because when «بين» is in the position of the nominative it is put in the nominative, as one says بينُ عينيه أحمر ("between his eyes is red"), putting «بين» in the nominative.

nahhas-irab:68-68.t: «وَمَنْ يَفْعَلْ ذلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثاماً»: a condition and its requital.

nahhas-irab:69-69.t: «يُضاعَفْ لَهُ الْعَذابُ» is a badal (substitute) for «يلق». Sībawayh said: because the doubling of the punishment is the meeting of «الأنام». [Translator's note: «لقيّ الأنام» is translated as printed; «لقيّ الآثام» ("the meeting of the penalty"), as below, is evidently meant.] ʿĀṣim read «يضاعف له العذاب يوم القيامة ويخلد فيها مهانا» in the nominative; the jussive is preferable for the reason we have mentioned. There are two views on the nominative: one is that it is cut off from what precedes; the other is that it is construed according to the sense, as if someone said: "What is the meeting of the penalty?", and it was said: "The punishment will be doubled for him."

nahhas-irab:70-70.t: «إِلَّا مَنْ تابَ» is in the position of the accusative as an exception. «فَأُوْلئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ اللَّهُ سَيِّئاتِهِمْ حَسَناتٍ»: two objects. We have already mentioned its meaning. Among the good things said about it is that "believer" is written in place of "unbeliever", and "obedient" in place of "disobedient".

nahhas-irab:71-71.t: «فَإِنَّهُ يَتُوبُ إِلَى اللَّهِ مَتاباً» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) carrying the sense of emphasis.

nahhas-irab:74-74.t: «قُرَّةَ أَعْيُنٍ» is not put in the plural because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun); had it been put in the plural to denote the different kinds, it would be permissible. «وَاجْعَلْنا لِلْمُتَّقِينَ إِماماً»: a singular indicating a plural.

nahhas-irab:75-75.t: «وَيُلَقَّوْنَ فِيها تَحِيَّةً وَسَلاماً»: this is the reading of the people of Medina and the people of Basra. The people of Kufa read «وَيُلَقَّوْنَ فِيها» [i.e. ويَلْقَوْنَ]. [Translator's note: both readings are printed identically in the source; the Kufan reading is ويَلْقَوْن.] Al-Farrāʾ said: «ويَلقون» is more pleasing to me, because if the reading were «يُلقَّون», it would in Arabic be with the bāʾ. This is a worse mistake than what has passed in the sūra, because he claims that if it were «يُلقَّون», it would in Arabic be بتحية وسلام ("with greeting and peace"). He said: just as one says "so-and-so is met (yatalaqqā) with peace and with good". Among the strange things in this is that he said يتلقّى, while the verse has «يُلقَّون», and the difference between them is clear, because one says فلان يتلقّى بالجنّة and the bāʾ may not be omitted — so how can this resemble that? Stranger still is that in the Qur'an there is «وَلَقَّاهُمْ نَضْرَةً وَسُرُوراً» [al-Insān: 11], which may not be read otherwise; and this makes clear that the preferable view is the opposite of what he said.

nahhas-irab:77-77.t: «فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزاماً»: it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās with a sound chain of transmission that he read «فقد كذّب الكافرون فسوف يكون لزاما» ("the unbelievers have denied, so it will be inseparable"). Likewise Shuʿba related it from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī from Abū al-Zubayr. Shuʿba said: and so it is in the reading of ʿAbdallāh ibn Masʿūd. This reading contradicts the muṣḥaf and ought to be taken as exegesis, because the meaning of «فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ» is that the unbelievers are addressed by it. And this reading [i.e. the canonical one], besides agreeing with the written text (al-sawād), is more fitting to the context of the speech, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: «قُلْ ما يَعْبَؤُا بِكُمْ رَبِّي لَوْلا دُعاؤُكُمْ», which is an address, and likewise «فَقَدْ كَذَّبْتُمْ فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزاماً»; so this is preferable to «فقد كذّب الكافرون فسوف يكون لزاما». The grammarians have discussed it, and among the good things said about it is that the construction is "the denial will be", because «كذبتم» indicates the denial; and its real sense in Arabic is "the requital of the denial will be an inseparable punishment", i.e. one possessed of inseparability (lizām). Lizām and mulāzama are one and the same. Abū Ḥātim related from Abū Zayd: I heard Qaʿnab Abū al-Sammāl read «فَسَوْفَ يَكُونُ لِزاماً» with fatḥa on the lām [i.e. لَزاما]. Abū Jaʿfar said: it would be the maṣdar (verbal noun) of لزم; the kasra is preferable, like qitāl and muqātala, just as they agreed on the kasra in His saying, Mighty and Majestic, «وَلَوْلا كَلِمَةٌ سَبَقَتْ مِنْ رَبِّكَ لَكانَ لِزاماً وَأَجَلٌ مُسَمًّى» [Ṭā Hā: 129]. Al-Farrāʾ has another view on the noun of «يكون»; he said: there is an unspecified [pronoun] (majhūl) in it. This is a mistake, because the khabar (predicate) of the majhūl can only be a clause, as He, Mighty and Majestic, said: «إِنَّهُ مَنْ يَتَّقِ وَيَصْبِرْ» [Yūsuf: 90], and as the grammarians relate: كان زيد منطلق ("it was: Zayd is departing"), with a majhūl in «كان», and the mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar being the predicate of the majhūl, the construction being "the matter was". As for saying كان منطلقا with a majhūl in «كان», that is not permissible according to anyone we know.
